summary: Standards: jcs refuses a 64-bit integer beyond 2^53-1 read from text, but an integer written with more digits than 64 bits hold (18446744073709551616 and up, or 9007199254740994 written as 9007199254740994.0) is read by serde as a double and written as its rounded double without an error, and so is a double built in code (Number::from_f64(9007199254740994.0) is 9007199254740994 while the text 9007199254740994 is refused). The module docs say so, and ATIP's README warns of it, but a plan whose input silently rounds gives the same digest for two different values; the crate cannot tell them apart after parsing. I fuzzed the number writer against JavaScript String() on 101793 doubles (random bits, powers of ten, near-ties): 0 differences, and the nine vendored vectors are byte-identical to the v1.2.1 tag (f61f2e02). Blast radius: canon-0-35-plan-jcs; canon's plan inputs are counts and digests, and must put anything above 2^53 in as a string.
